thread.title: Everything Apple just announced at its Mac and iPad Pro event - MarketWatch

author: Emily Bary
title: Everything Apple just announced at its Mac and iPad Pro event - MarketWatch
text:
Apple Inc. unveiled pricey upgrades to its iPad Pro and Mac lines at an event in Brooklyn, N.Y., on Tuesday, as well as releasing an enhanced version of its Apple Pencil stylus.
Coming into the event, Apple AAPL, +0.25% hadn’t refreshed the MacBook Air ’s design since 2010. The device got a series of enhancements on Tuesday, including a thinner profile, reduced bezels, retina display and a varied color palette.
Apple’s new retina MacBook Air has a 13.3-inch screen and a backlit “butterfly” keyboard. It’s the first Air device to feature Touch ID fingerprint recognition or a Force Touch trackpad, which the company said boasts a 20% larger area relative to the trackpad on the older model. It’s 15.6 millimeters thin and features an eighth-generation Intel Inc. Core i5 processor. The device can play movies for up to 13 hours nonstop.

The Air starts at $1,199 for a 128-gigabyte model. The previous-generation model started at $999 and will still be on sale for that price. A new 264 GB version will go for $1,399. The new Airs have two USB-C ports, which handle charging and all other connectivity, whereas the older models connected via traditional USB and a dedicated charging port.
The new models are available for preorder and will hit stores on Nov. 7.
Apple also spruced up the Mac mini , a small desktop computer that requires users to supply their own monitor. A revamped version of the device has configurable memory of up to 64GB. Storage configurations start at 128GB and can be configured up to 2 terabytes, according to Apple’s website.
The company said that its new Mac mini has a space gray finish and many connectivity options, including four USB-C ports, two traditional USB ports, an HDMI port, and an Ethernet port. It starts at $799, compared with a $499 base price for the prior-generation version.
On the tablet side, Apple introduced a new 11-inch iPad Pro and upgraded the 12.9-inch Pro . Apple fit an 11-inch screen into the same body as the previous 10.5-inch model by reducing the bezels on the device. Apple also packed a 12.9-inch screen into a smaller device, which Apple said is now about the size of a piece of 8.5-inch by 11-inch notebook paper.
While previous iPads charged with Apple’s Lightning cable, the new models will connect via USB-C, and they’ll allow users to charge their iPhones through the iPad.
See more: Apple introduces new iPad Pro, Apple Pencil
The company said this is the first iPad Pro line to feature Apple’s latest-generation neural engine, which allows the device to handle 5 trillion operations each second. It’s also the first iPad family to feature FaceID, which lets users unlock their devices with their face and also enables Apple’s animated “Memoji,” digital avatars that bear likeness to their user.
The devices, as with the new computers, are up for preorder now and officially go on sale Nov. 7. The 11-inch Wi-Fi model starts at $799, while the 12.9-inch version will begin at $999. Adding cellular connectivity makes the devices more expensive: A 1TB cellular version goes for $1,899.
Prior to the announcement, Apple sold a 10.5-inch iPad Pro for a base price of $649 and a 12.9-inch model for a starting price of $799.
Read: iPhone XR creates some drama for Apple’s new lineup
At the Tuesday event, the company also enhanced its Apple Pencil stylus . The new version will attach magnetically to the iPad, charge wirelessly, and pair automatically with the device. Users will have the ability to change between functions by double tapping on the Pencil. This newest model will sell for $129 and features an option for “laser engraving,” while the original pencil sells for $99. Apple will continue to offer that model as well, given that the new Pencil is only compatible with its latest line of iPad Pros.
Apple shares were little changed in midday Tuesday trading. The stock has gained 27% over the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.43% of which Apple is a component, has gained 5.2%.
